summary: Streaming resume duplicates function-call webhooks when idempotency header is rewritten by edge proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicated external webhook invocations for server-side function_call events after a client stream reconnect/resume. The original function call appears to complete on our runtime but the webhook gets invoked twice when the client retries the streaming session.

Impact:
- Customer (NimbusPayments) sees duplicate payment-create webhooks resulting in duplicated downstream jobs (idempotency not respected by downstream).
- Occurs intermittently during poor mobile network conditions when the browser/edge SDK reconnects mid-stream.
- Potential financial impact for customer: duplicate charge attempts and manual reconciliation.

Environment:
- Customer using TypeScript browser SDK v1.12.0 with streaming chat + function_call enabled.
- Dedicated deployment, prod us-east region, API fronted by CloudFront-like edge layer.
- Server runtime: serving-runtime v2.7.3, api-gateway v1.9.1.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Open streaming chat session from mobile web client and trigger a sequence that results in a function_call to the payment webhook (function name: create_payment).
2) Simulate a flaky network (toggle airplane mode) so the socket disconnects during the streaming/chunked response (server had already emitted a function_call and partial response).
3) Client reconnects and the SDK attempts to resume the stream with a fresh resume attempt; SDK sets an idempotency header (x-idempotency-key) on the resumed connection.
4) Observe two webhook POSTs for create_payment within seconds.

Expected behavior:
- Only a single create_payment webhook should be delivered for the original function_call. SDK retries/resume should not cause duplicate downstream side effects when an idempotency key is provided.

Actual behavior:
- Two POSTs reach customer's webhook endpoint. The first is the original in-flight delivery from the runtime. The second comes after the resumed connection and appears to be triggered by a resumed function_call state.

Observed logs (redacted):
- Runtime logs show request traces T-9a7e... and T-9a7e... (same trace) with function_call recorded once, but gateway access logs show two separate incoming streaming requests with different idempotency header values: 
  - req1: x-idempotency-key: "8e4b24f6-7a9e-4c3d-9f2a-aaaaaaa..."
  - req2: x-idempotency-key: "8e4b24f6-7a9e-4c3d-9f2a-1"  (note numeric suffix)
- Edge logs (CloudFront) show header normalization/truncation events when header length > 48 chars; downstream origin receives rewritten header name/value for second request.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Advise customer to include a per-call confirmation token in the webhook payload (client-side generated) and to deduplicate on the webhook receiver while we investigate.
- As an immediate mitigation, asked customer to increase server-side idempotency window and to enable "webhook delivery dedupe" via a short-lived token if possible.

Root cause hypothesis so far:
- Edge proxy is rewriting or truncating the x-idempotency-key header on connection resume (some internal normalization rule at the CDN that appends/truncates long header values), causing our gateway to treat the resumed request as a distinct idempotent scope. The runtime reconciles function_call state but the gateway's idempotency lookup uses the altered key, so the resumed request triggers an additional webhook delivery.

Data points collected / logs attached:
- Access logs and header captures from edge for the two attempts (attached as support artifact).
- Server trace showing single function_call state but duplicate webhook deliveries downstream.
- Customer-provided webhook receiver logs showing two POST requests within 2s.

Proposed next steps / remediation:
1) Short term (0-24h): Document and push the recommended customer workaround (embed client-confirmation token in webhook payload and dedupe).
2) Fix the gateway to canonicalize idempotency keys from either header or streaming-metadata and accept alternate name forms (x-idempotency-key and x-idempotency). Backfill support for keys truncated by edge (map detected rewritten forms to canonical token using a best-effort normalization).
3) SDK change (TS/browser): On resume attempt, include idempotency token in both header and in the first JSON control frame body so origin sees the same token even if an edge alters headers. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/842 (WIP).
4) Long term: Add signed confirmation tokens on function_call completion so webhook consumers can validate original call provenance.

Notes:
- This issue is reproducible with a synthetic test using our edge staging where we simulate header truncation; reproduction script and test harness stored on the linked Confluence page.
- We should coordinate with CDN partner to remove header normalization rules for this header or increase header length allowance.
investigation_notes: Engineering ran correlation of traces across gateway, runtime and webhook delivery. Found mismatch between idempotency header observed at edge vs origin. Confirmed SDK sets a UUID v4 token; edge truncated to 37 chars and appended a suffix in some cases. Reproduced in staging by injecting header-mod rewrite. Eng hypothesis: CDN rule intended to canonicalize headers containing control chars is accidentally mangling long IDs. Next step: file ticket with infra/CDN partner and push gateway fallback normalization. Temporary SDK/console guidance added.

resolution: In Progress - mitigation applied. SDK patch and gateway normalization hotfix planned and in review.
workaround: 1) Add client-generated confirmation token to webhook payload and dedupe on receiver. 2) If using a custom CDN, disable header normalization for x-idempotency-key or increase header length allowance. 3) Use the SDK patch (1.12.1) when released which writes idempotency token into control frame body as well as header.
next_steps: - Complete SDK PR review and ship 1.12.1. - Deploy gateway normalization hotfix to prod-us-east. - Engage CDN partner to remove/adjust header rewrite rule. - Follow up with NimbusPayments by 2026-03-18 with rollout plan and expected ETA.
customer_impact_summary: High: duplicate downstream payments observed; customer performing manual reconciliation; requests a permanent server-side fix.
priority_rationale: P1 due to financial impact and production customer data loss/duplication risk.
notes_for_internal_runbook: When a streaming resume is reported with duplicated function_call side effects, capture edge header snapshots, compare header values between edge and origin, and check for CDN header rewrite rules. Apply SDK fallback to embed idempotency token in body for immediate mitigation.
public_response_snippet: Thanks Danielle — we’ve identified an edge-level header rewrite that can cause resumed streams to present a different idempotency token. We’ve provided a temporary dedupe workaround and are shipping an SDK + gateway patch in the next 72 hours. We will follow up with a detailed rollout plan.
